title: Question Mark Above Line

illustrates.quote: Answer Cues with Question Marks. Follow print when a question mark is shown standing alone representing a write-on-line. When print uses both a question mark and a low line or dash, ignore the question mark and use the underscore or dash. Insert a transcriber’s note explaining this usage.

blocks.text: Print shows a question mark over an underscore. In braille, the question mark is omitted.

print.printFeatures: A question mark is printed directly above a write-on-line underscore.

braille.notes: Independently re-extracted from source (fixed left margin / line-number field stripped by counting; U+2800→space; trailing spaces removed); confirmed byte-identical to both run A and run B (gold-10-A/gold-10-B) except where differences.md records a correction.

resolution: Braille matches both A and B exactly. Print unchanged from A/B; the TN wording is the given braille’s own note, back-translated.
